title: Pulsars: Cosmic Lighthouses
objective: After this level you can explain what pulsars are and how they were discovered.
summary: Pulsars are spinning neutron stars whose beams sweep past Earth. Jocelyn Bell Burnell discovered the first in 1967.

cards.headline: A signal so regular it was nicknamed “LGM”: little green men.
cards.body: In 1967 a radio telescope picked up a pulse that ticked like a clock. It wasn’t aliens.

cards.headline: Lighthouses in space
cards.body: A pulsar is a spinning neutron star that sends out beams of radio waves. Each time a beam sweeps past Earth, we see a pulse, just like a lighthouse. Some pulsars spin hundreds of times every second.

cards.headline: The discovery
cards.body: The first pulsar was discovered in 1967 by Jocelyn Bell Burnell, then a graduate student, while studying radio signals. The pulses were so regular that her team briefly considered, half-jokingly, that they might be artificial.

cards.fact: The Crab Nebula has a pulsar at its heart.
cards.context: The nebula is the remains of a supernova that Chinese astronomers recorded in 1054.
